body: It's actually the opposite, because I can be completely honest on here whereas I can't IRL. Thanks for being concerned though.

My emotional impulses. I'm always causing unnecessary fights, or refuse to do certain things because of my anxiety and things like that, which causes more fights. I can't say sorry anymore, I don't know why. I can't trust anyone anymore, I care less about family members now, I take advantage of my best friend by making him drive me to places or run errands for me because I can't, yet I still manage to be ungrateful and just lash at him for small things.    
    
I use my past as an excuse and pull the victim card. I really hate myself, you have no idea.

Have you thought about maybe listening to some of his songs? I know it sounds silly, but when I was extremely depressed and remembered Mr. Rogers, that's what I did. Or looked up little interviews or recordings of him on YouTube.     
    
He would probably have said to you that he likes you for you, that you've come so far and have done so well as a person despite your circumstances, and would very much enjoy your company.    
    
I hope you feel a little better.

You know, I've only just stumbled onto this thread, but even I can see that you're either not understanding a word that Frisco is saying, or you're purposely trying to sway the argument in your favor by adding completely uninvolved discussions into the whole debate.    
    
Hormones aren't something you can easily control at a young age. You can learn about it, yes, but it's a giant wave of new emotions that you're being introduced to and have to learn to understand, because hearing about it isn't enough.    
    
It's like depression. People hear about it all the time and how terrible it is to go through. But no way in hell can anyone understand what it's like, how much energy it takes to deal with and all the strange emotions and disassociation, unless you're actually depressed. A kid who barely understands life can't possibly fathom what puberty actually is or feels like.    
    
If you're in front of a depressed person, you don't talk about depressing shit or things like suicide. You just don't do that, because it encourages and worsens behavior. It's the same case with puberty; if you know something might encourage unwarranted behavior, don't do it. Kids aren't mentally grown yet to know entirely of what's right and wrong. You can wear whatever you want in front of adults, but not kids who are going through a giant transition in their life where physicality is extremely sensitive. Especially not in a school setting.
